title: Tobal 2
subtitle: A larger world behind the fighting arena
summary: Tobal 2 is DreamFactory's PlayStation fighting game, released in Japan on 25 April 1997. It expands the original's combination of three-dimensional duels and dungeon exploration, retaining characters designed by Akira Toriyama. Fighters move around one another while keeping their attention on the opponent, using high, middle and low attacks alongside grappling and defence. The sequel adds more possibilities without abandoning that physical relationship. body: Tobal 2 is DreamFactory's PlayStation fighting game, released in Japan on 25 April 1997. It expands the original's combination of three-dimensional duels and dungeon exploration, retaining characters designed by Akira Toriyama. Fighters move around one another while keeping their attention on the opponent, using high, middle and low attacks alongside grappling and defence. The sequel adds more possibilities without abandoning that physical relationship. Its greatly enlarged Quest mode makes the arena part of a wider activity, encouraging the player to explore and build a collection as well as win the next conventional match.

Quest mode gives the fighting system a longer structure, with a large roster available through progress and discoveries. The expanded cast offers many different bodies through which to learn the same underlying rules. A new fireball attack gives each character another option, while movement and close grappling remain important. The player still has to decide when to advance, circle or hold a defensive position. The size of the collection becomes meaningful because another unlocked fighter can change the practical feel of confronting a familiar opponent, rather than serving only as another name on a selection screen.

Seiichi Ishii returned as director, with Takayuki Nakamura composing the music. The game improved its character shading and resolution while retaining smooth sixty-frame-per-second action. It launched alongside Sony's Dual Analog Controller in Japan and supported the new peripheral. Unlike Tobal No. 1, it was not released internationally. Its two hundred playable characters later gave it a record-setting reputation, but its distinctive appeal also lies in the expanded Quest mode: the fighting game becomes something to inhabit over time, with discoveries continuing beyond the next tournament victory.

Bring another opponent into the collection
A sequel that stayed in Japan
